requirements.text: When renameCategory is called for a default category, it must update every saved receipt whose category name matches the old name case‑insensitively to the new name.
When renameCategory is called for a custom category, it must update every saved receipt whose category name matches the old name case‑insensitively to the new name.
After a successful rename, getAllCategories must no longer list the old category name.
After a successful rename, syncCategoriesWithReceipts must not re‑add the old category name.
After a successful rename, isCategoryInUse(newName) must return true when any receipt previously used the old name.
When renameCategory succeeds, all other fields of each updated receipt (date, amount, notes, etc.) must remain unchanged.
If renameCategory fails because the new name is invalid, no receipt categories are changed.
If renameCategory fails because the new name already exists, no receipt categories are changed.
If renameCategory fails because the original category is not found, no receipt categories are changed.
validateMileageMiles must return true for any numeric value > 0 with at most one decimal place (e.g., 12.5).
validateMileageMiles must return false for zero, negative numbers, numbers with more than one decimal place (e.g., 12.55), and non‑numeric text.
The Miles input field on the Add mileage screen must accept the string "12.5" as valid input.
When a decimal mileage value (e.g., 12.5) is entered, the displayed deduction amount must be calculated using the exact decimal value.
When a decimal mileage value is saved, the stored mileage record must retain the decimal value (e.g., 12.5) without rounding.
